To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a three-dimensional hydrogels supports clonal growth and maintenance of Sox2-positive and Sox2-negative dermal papilla cells in vitro; 2) Sox2 expression is maintained, but not induced in Sox2-negative cells in vitro or vivo; 3) Sox2-negative cells are less efficient at forming spheres than Sox2-positive cells, but have greater ability to contribute to dermal papilla and non-dermal papilla cells of reconstituted hair follicles
Sox2+ cells can be maintained in culture and are a distinct cell lineage, and Sox2− cells have a greater potential to form dermal papillae in vivo than Sox2+ cells.

we developed a novel culture system for clonal expansion of DP cells that supports the maintenance of two distinct DP cell types and their ability to contribute to the DP in vivo, and that we identified Sox2+ cells as a distinct DP cell lineage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Sox2 in hair follicle development and maintenance and its role in the regulation of stem cell fate.
the role of the dermal papilla in hair morphogenesis.
the development of an in vitro system for the clonal growth of dermal papillae (DP) and the study of their intrinsic and extrinsic regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper provides a novel and interesting model for the clonal growth of dermal papillae cells.
Sox2+ and Sox2− DP are distinct populations of cells, and that Sox2 is a marker of DP cells that is not necessarily required for their function in vivo.
this study has provided a novel method for culturing and maintaining the two distinct dermal papilla cell populations that exist in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Sox2 is a key regulator of dermal papillary cells, and that Sox2+ dermal papillary stem cells can be isolated from mouse neonatal skin.
Sox2+ dermal papillae (DP) are a distinct cellular population, and that Sox2 is a useful marker of DP identity in vitro and in vivo.
we have identified a three-dimensional culture system that supports the clonal growth of neonatal dermal papilla cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed an in vitro culture system for clonal growth of dermal papillae (DP) cells from neonatal mouse skin that supports the growth of Sox2+ and Sox2− DP cells.
the Sox2+ DP are a distinct cell lineage, and they are not a subset of Sox2− DP.
the dermal papilla cells that give rise to guard/awl/augene and zigzag hair follicles are clonally distinct.
